title: Fort Laramie
paragraphs: An adult Western drama set around a U.S. Army post on the frontier, following soldiers and civilians through the dangers, hardships, and moral conflicts of life in the West.

Adult frontier Western centered on Captain Lee Quince and the soldiers/civilians around a U.S. Army post. The frozen set contains the 1955 audition plus all 40 numbered 1956 broadcasts; the Sep. 23 broadcast repeats the Feb. 12 Woman at Horse Creek recording.
GRH documents the program through CBS regular run (January 22, 1956 to October 28, 1956) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|raymond-burr|Raymond Burr]] (performer on 40 recordings), Kathleen Hite (writer on 26 recordings), Norman Macdonnell (producer on 19 recordings and director on 18 recordings), Amerigo Moreno (music supervisor on 17 recordings), Bill James (sound patterns on 17 recordings), [[person|jack-moyles|Jack Moyles]] (performer on 16 recordings), and [[person|john-dehner|John Dehner]] (performer on 16 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.86a7ba0f309a63c9|WEEI]] (aircheck from station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include frontier Army-post life, military duty and discipline, soldier-civilian frontier relations, family, wives and widows at the post, recruits, training and soldiering, and stagecoach, scouting and frontier travel.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Adult Western drama in late-network radio, Frontier Army-post setting, 1950s radio portrayals of Native/frontier relations, and CBS sustaining drama.
